# Preserve bounded native startup diagnostics without changing acceptance

Real packaged city checks compiled successfully but timed out with zero ready
operations and frames. Executor projection retained assertions and a terminal
timeout code, but discarded the verifier's renderer/console errors, page probes
and actual window flags. Those old outputs cannot establish which startup step
stalled. Repeated model edits cannot repair missing host evidence.

Retain a bound, diagnostic-only text log within the existing immutable native job
output. Keep the strict Core schema: one optional string, with a 64 KiB UTF-8
limit, rather than accepting the raw renderer object. Executor projection checks
all four native identities, bounds and redacts selected values, marks truncation
and prioritizes first causes and phase transitions. Missing fields in older
outputs remain missing; no backfill, automatic retry or verdict changes occur.

The verifier records stage start/completion/failure and elapsed time separately
from acceptance assertions. It retains the existing 30-second check deadline.
Diagnostics help distinguish artifact work, runtime-server creation, window
construction, navigation and ready handshake. They do not authorize candidate
adoption, source writes or model continuation.

Validation covers stage failure with no window, ready timeout after navigation,
full console tails, foreign evidence, UTF-8 bounds, redaction, Core serialization
and unchanged pass/fail through the real executor with a fixture native verifier.
Actual packaged validation remains a separate coordinator-controlled run.
